chief_complaint: Cardiovascular risk management and uncontrolled hypertension follow-up
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 61-year-old male with a history of an acute NSTEMI in 2009 and ongoing secondary‑prevention therapy. Despite being on three antihypertensive agents (hydrochlorothiazide, losartan, metoprolol) his blood pressure remains stage 2 (144/96 mmHg) and heart rate is 94 bpm. He is obese (BMI ≥30) and reports chronic stress. Social factors include unstable housing, low educational attainment, a history of intimate‑partner abuse, and a criminal record, all of which may impede adherence. Recent visits have been largely wellness‑focused with no recent cardiac imaging or laboratory assessments, and several key labs (lipids, A1c, eGFR) are missing. Medication list shows dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin + prasugrel) continued beyond the typical 12‑month period, a low‑dose statin, and duplicate hydrochlorothiazide entries.

active_problems.name: Acute non-ST segment elevation myocardial infarction

past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include colon polyp, prior ankle sprain, acute bronchitis, gingivitis, dental caries, and episodes of stress that have resolved. The patient also has a long-standing history of low educational attainment, military service, and housing instability. No chronic systemic diseases other than those listed as active were documented.

risk_factor_summary: Stage 2 hypertension (144/96 mmHg) despite three antihypertensives, obesity (BMI ≥30), prior NSTEMI and ongoing dual antiplatelet therapy, low‑intensity statin, and elevated resting heart rate (94 bpm) indicate very high cardiovascular risk. Missing key laboratory data (BMI, A1c, eGFR, lipid panel) limits risk stratification. Polypharmacy risk is moderate; duplicate hydrochlorothiazide entry noted. Social determinants (housing, education, abuse, criminal record) further increase risk for poor disease control and adverse outcomes.
